hunks.baseline: Perhaps thanks to his diligent round-the-clock operation, the name Jang Sam the Heavenly Axe had eventually become fairly well known.
hunks.sol: Perhaps thanks to his diligent round-the-clock operation, the name Heavenly Axe Jang Sam had eventually become fairly well known.

hunks.baseline: Today was no different. He had risen before dawn and set out to work with his five loyal underlings, the Five-Colored Ghosts… but for some reason, his feet simply refused to stop.
hunks.sol: Today was no different. He had risen before dawn and set out to work with his five loyal underlings, the Five-Colored Ghosts… but for some reason, he couldn’t stop walking.

hunks.baseline: Had a ghost possessed him? Jang Sam was bewildered, but the moment he saw the luxurious four-horse carriage, his professional instincts came roaring back to life.
hunks.sol: Had he been bewitched by a ghost? Jang Sam was bewildered, but the moment he saw the luxurious four-horse carriage, his professional instincts came roaring back to life.

hunks.baseline: But it would take more than that to make me blink. I’d spent seven years as a Hunter and been through every kind of battle imaginable—even aerial combat.
hunks.sol: But it would take more than that to make me blink. I’d spent seven years as a Hunter and been through battles on land, at sea, and even in the air.

hunks.baseline: “Why? Unless they belong to a sizable mountain stronghold, attacking a martial family is practically suicide. Robbing people in the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s own backyard… I wonder what kind of reckless fools they are.”
hunks.sol: “Why? Unless they belong to a sizable mountain stronghold, attacking a Murim family is practically suicide. Robbing people in the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s own backyard… I wonder what kind of reckless fools they are.”

hunks.baseline: The coachman's unflappable attitude practically screamed that he was a master. Just like now.
hunks.sol: The coachman’s unflappable attitude practically screamed that he was a master. Just like now.

hunks.baseline: *Damn, that aura.*
hunks.sol: *Damn, what presence.*

hunks.baseline: “They won’t shed tears until they see the coffin. To think they would dare block your path! They’ll pay dearly for failing to recognize a master.”
hunks.sol: “They’re the kind who won’t cry until they see the coffin. To think they would dare block your path! They’ll pay dearly for failing to recognize a master.”

hunks.baseline: The coachman’s pupils began to tremble. It was an earthquake measuring 8.0 on the Richter scale.
hunks.sol: The coachman’s pupils began to tremble. It was an 8.0-magnitude earthquake.

hunks.baseline: The coachman stared at me with the expression of a man who had lost his country, then collapsed like an inflatable toy with the air let out of it.
hunks.sol: The coachman stared at me with the expression of a man who had lost his country, then collapsed like a deflated inflatable toy.

hunks.baseline: “Ha-ha! Ha-ha-ha!”
hunks.sol: “Ha! Ha-ha-ha!”

hunks.baseline: The bandits shrieked with laughter. My back was already damp with cold sweat, and I hadn’t even noticed when it started.
hunks.sol: The bandits roared with laughter. My back was already damp with cold sweat, and I hadn’t even noticed when it started.

hunks.baseline: I couldn’t bring myself to say the word *death*. I swallowed it instead.
hunks.sol: I couldn’t bring myself to say the word *death*. I swallowed hard.

hunks.baseline: I stood there dazed for a moment, until an axe came flying at me and snapped me back to reality. They had the numbers, and they were launching a preemptive attack too?
hunks.sol: I stood there dazed for a moment until an axe came flying at me and snapped me back to reality. They had the numbers, and they were launching a preemptive attack too?

hunks.baseline: The axe slammed into the ground ten meters in front of me. No—it flopped over. The bandit who had thrown it scratched the back of his head sheepishly.
hunks.sol: The axe struck the ground a good ten meters short of me. No—it didn’t even stick. It toppled over. The bandit who had thrown it scratched the back of his head sheepishly.

hunks.baseline: “Should I have thrown it a little higher?”
hunks.sol: “Should I have aimed a little higher?”

hunks.baseline: A few of them looked confused by my gesture of surrender, while the Heavenly Axe smiled proudly, like a father watching his son return from military service.
hunks.sol: A few of them looked confused by my gesture of surrender, while the Heavenly Axe smiled proudly, like a father welcoming his son home from military service.

hunks.baseline: With a steady stride and balanced posture. One breath per step. My breath escaped my mouth in white clouds that pierced the dawn air.
hunks.sol: With a steady stride and balanced posture. One breath per step. My breath streamed out into the dawn air.

hunks.baseline: My heart pounded. At the same time, a warning stirred in the back of my mind.
hunks.sol: My heart pounded. At the same time, caution stirred in the back of my mind.

hunks.baseline: For seven years, I had fought every single day. I was a competitor—and a martial artist called a Hunter.
hunks.sol: For seven years, I had fought every single day. I was a gambler with my life on the line—and a martial artist called a Hunter.
Then came the final step.

hunks.baseline: I shot straight forward. The ground sank beneath my foot, and the sound followed after me. In that frozen moment, the Heavenly Axe’s mouth slowly fell open.
hunks.sol: I shot straight forward. The ground cratered beneath my foot, and the sound followed after me. In that frozen moment, the Heavenly Axe’s mouth slowly fell open.

hunks.baseline: The corners of my mouth lifted before I knew it.
hunks.sol: I found myself grinning.
